- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤-0.5) or volatile, model often underestimates downside risk; add 1–3% buffer to forecast for downward correction.
- Model consistently overpredicts 30-day peaks after recent spikes; cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak observed in prior 5–7 days.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, model fails to adjust; apply mean reversion to forecast by subtracting 0.5–1.5% per day of sentiment decay.
- Forecast errors are more pronounced in early 30-day window (days 1–7); apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% for first 7 days if sentiment is neutral or mixed.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “high-low” oscillations, model tends to lag; forecast should be adjusted upward by 0.5–1.0% for each 2–3 day sentiment cycle.
